### 🟡 Changes recommended The decoding-failure path without a failure consumer lacks an agent-backed regression.
1 open issue - [Add regression test for chunked-query decoding failure capture](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20703#discussion_r4320869073) · New
3 resolved since last review - [Preserve user exceptions thrown after cancellation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20703#discussion_r4310130698) - [Report intentional pre-response cancellation as success](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20703#discussion_r4310130680) - [Register and label the exception-log test profile](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20703#discussion_r4310130658)
Review effort: Balanced

[Testing] The new regressions do not exercise the decoding-failure path this advice adds: `FAILURE` is valid JSON containing a server-reported error, and user callback exceptions are captured separately by the wrappers. Losing this advice's failure capture could therefore go undetected. Add an agent-backed chunked-query regression in `InfluxDbQueryLifecycleTest` with an invalid query-result shape and no failure consumer. Assert exactly one ERROR span and one duration observation, both with the decoding exception's `error.type`, and include it in the latest-dependency run to cover the newer-client behavior described here.

Splits the InfluxDB changes from #20685, correcting query outcomes and duration timing without changing other integrations.

- **Error classification:** Classify HTTP-200 top-level and per-statement errors with bounded `error.type`, never raw error text. Retain available HTTP error codes.
- **Terminal completion:** End asynchronous and chunked operations exactly once after callbacks and chunk processing finish, retaining callback, transport, and decoding failures, including newer-client decoding failures without a failure consumer.
- **Cancellation and compatibility:** Make the call available before failure consumers run so pre-response cancellation remains successful. Preserve `DONE` handling, callback parent context, and supported 2.4 APIs.
- **Regression coverage:** Cover synchronous response errors, one asynchronous statement error, successful and failed chunked completion, cancellation before and after response delivery, callback failures after cancellation, and a single 2.4 statement-error case, with span and duration-metric assertions. Retain HTTP `400` assertions in the existing failing-query integration test.
metadata.title: Fix InfluxDB query error classification and async completion
